pairs.question: Is g.issuer redundant because the append channel only admits owner-issued grants, or can a non-owner mint an approval that the publish gate honours?
pairs.W0: approval row for try-a at its current revision written by the owner
pairs.W1: the same row written by an agent session with `distribute.py approve`
pairs.D1: publish inadmissible (self-issued is not an owner approval)
pairs.method: scratch worktree of f2249c1, no credentials, no push: run `approve` as the agent, then `publish --dry-run`; read every precondition in dispatch_preconditions for an issuer check; search the tests and the manifest for any check on who wrote approvals.json
pairs.expected: the dry run prints the publish requests for the self-minted approval; no precondition reads the issuer; the only barriers left are a clean pushed tree, which any claude/* branch satisfies, and possession of the four X credentials. The mechanism collapses the pair, so issuer is EARNED as a verifiable binding, not as a prose field

pairs.question: Can the same check on the same subject return different verdicts under a legitimate environment change, so that v.environment (or a hermeticity rule) is earned?
pairs.W0: scripts/verify_claims.py at f2249c1 run in this container, behind the egress proxy
pairs.W1: the same script at the same commit run by GitHub Actions (verify.yml, run of 2026-09-21)
pairs.D0: support URLs verified (the subject is unchanged)
pairs.kind: control-like: the correct decision is the same in both worlds; the check must not differ
pairs.method: compare the per-claim support-URL verdicts in both environments; probe one failing URL here and read who answered (proxy or origin); fetch the same bytes by another route to show the subject exists
pairs.expected: 11 support URLs FAIL here with HTTP 403 and PASS in CI; the 403 is written by the proxy, not the origin; the verdict depends on the environment. Either v.environment is recorded, or environment-caused access failures are classified UNEVALUABLE so that PASS/FAIL stay environment-independent

pairs.question: Do the owner-side records (13.05 Prompt Intake, Freeze Ledger, Execution Receipts; 13.11 MARD) bind a receipt to the exact bytes dispatched?
pairs.W0: draft D frozen twice (v1, then v2 superseding it); v1 dispatched
pairs.D0: 13.10-style score of v1 applies to the run
pairs.D1: score of v1 does not apply
pairs.method: read the live 13.05 structure from its export (sha256 5605973e...); populate a local copy with both worlds using only the columns the sheet defines; compare the receipt rows; check MARD's task-identity fields
pairs.expected: the receipt rows are identical in both worlds: receipts carry DRAFT ID but no freeze id, version or digest; snapshots are mutable cells with no digest; MARD carries references, not digests. The existing record type does NOT close R9a, which withdraws E1's 'B + 13.05 = 15/15' claim. The smallest fix is one digest of the dispatched bytes on the receipt, matched against a digest on the freeze row, or dispatch bytes committed to git

decision_rules.earned: a field or rule is earned when the current mechanism gives the same decision on W0 and W1 where the correct decisions differ, and adding it restores the difference
decision_rules.withdraw: if X3 collapses, E1's claim that the owner-side 13.05 records carry R9a is withdrawn in the handoff, not silently corrected
